name: The Park Tower Knightsbridge
positioning: The Park Tower Knightsbridge, a Luxury Collection Hotel, London: a circular tower designed by Richard Seifert in Knightsbridge, with suites positioned for views over Hyde Park and the city, butler service in its suites and direct access to Knightsbridge Tube Station
best_for: Shoppers who want Harrods and Harvey Nichols a few minutes' walk away
Travelers who want a suite with city or Hyde Park views and a personal butler
Museum-goers who want to walk to the Victoria and Albert Museum

facts.text: The hotel has direct access to Knightsbridge Tube Station and the Piccadilly Line.
Harvey Nichols and Harrods are both within a few minutes' walk of the hotel.
The Victoria and Albert Museum and the Saatchi Gallery are within walking distance of the hotel.
Marble bathrooms have bathrobes and slippers, a heated vanity mirror, and walk-in showers with glass doors and bathtubs.
Suites booked with butler service include a packing and unpacking service.
The Lowndes Penthouse Suite is a two-bedroom suite, bordered by districts such as Belgravia.
The concierge team is led by a Clefs d'Or head concierge.
The chauffeur service offers a range of vehicles, with a footman if required.
Private training, Pilates and yoga sessions can be arranged at an additional charge.
Jogging maps of nearby Hyde Park are provided for guests who want to exercise outside.
The Hyde Bar offers over 130 international premium whiskies.
The Trianon, reserved for hotel guests' breakfast, has floor-to-ceiling windows looking onto the outdoor terrace.

highlights.text: The building's circular form and expansive windows were designed to showcase views across Hyde Park, Knightsbridge and London's landmarks.
The signature suites are positioned to capture sweeping views across the city, from Hyde Park and Westminster to Lowndes Square, Sloane Square and Knightsbridge.
The hotel was designed by British architect Richard Seifert and unveiled in 1973.
With The Park Tower Butler service, a personal butler contacts guests before arrival to plan their itinerary and handle special requests.
The Knightsbridge Lounge, where afternoon tea is served, has an 18-foot teardrop glass chandelier and a hand-painted canopy of magnolia blossom on draped silk.

considerations.text: The underground car park beneath the hotel is operated by a third party, Care Park, not by the hotel.
Afternoon tea must be booked 24 hours in advance.
WhataHotel notes the Knightsbridge area is busy, with high foot traffic.
